title: Customer assurance pathway and questionnaire accelerator
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: create a lightweight, repeatable pathway (the 'assurance accelerator') that shortens enterprise security and compliance intake from multiple weeks to a predictable SLA-driven flow. Scope includes: a triage rubric, prefilled questionnaire templates for common certifications (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA/GDPR/DPA), an SLA negotiation scaffolding for CSMs, and a small set of automation shims (answer suggestions, evidence bundler, and routing hints) to reduce manual effort.

Why now: top-of-funnel enterprise requests are a primary blocker for Dedicated/Private deals. Customers repeatedly ask for the same evidence and answers; duplicative work is increasing costs and time-to-contract. This initiative reduces time-to-first-yes, improves developer/SE throughput, and provides audit trails for compliance requests.

Key deliverables:
- Triage rubric: account risk -> intake lane mapping (fast-path / evidence-bundled / legal-review) with a clear SLA per lane.
- Questionnaire accelerator: curated templates + prefilled answer library (by certification and hosting mode) and an API to fetch suggested answers.
- SLA Negotiation Scaffolding: CSM facing one-pager + automated SLA estimator that surfaces expected time and required evidence.
- Evidence bundler: a serverless workflow that compiles docs (reports, encryption configs, region residency statements) into a single archive for customers.
- Admin console UI: lightweight panel showing intake status, assigned owner, elapsed SLA, and ability to escalate.
- Eval harness: sample prompts and test cases to validate answer accuracy and detect regressions when templates or product changes occur.

Success metrics:
- Reduce median intake-to-delivery time for common questionnaires by 60% within quarter.
- Increase percentage of fast-path requests completed without legal review from 18% to 50%.
- Reduce SE/CS hours spent per intake by 40%.

Out of scope for initial rollout: full legal negotiations, contract redlines, or automating policy exceptions. The first release targets evidence-assembly and routing; legal review remains human-in-the-loop for escalations.

Stakeholders: Product (Aisha Raman), Solution Engineering (Liam O'Connor), Security & Compliance (Priya Menon), Legal (Marco Alvarez), Customer Success (Tina Chen), Engineering owners: infra/runtime (Jared Kim) and ops (Nora Patel).

Risks and mitigations:
- Accuracy risk: suggested answers could be incorrect if product changes; mitigate with versioned templates + audit logs + required owner signoff for each answer.
- Over-automation risk: legal requirements vary by customer; mitigate by limiting automation to evidence bundling and suggested text, not automated acceptance.
- Maintenance cost: template drift; mitigate with quarterly review cadence owned by Security & Compliance.

Rollout plan:
- Alpha (2 weeks): internal SE/CS pilot with 5 active accounts; manual verification step on every response.
- Beta (4 weeks): open to qualifying self-serve customers and selected enterprise accounts; metrics dashboard enabled.
- GA (end of cycle): available to all accounts with documentation, runbook, and runbook-driven escalation patterns.

Acceptance criteria:
- Triage rubric implemented as a configurable rule set in the console.
- Template library seeded with SOC2, ISO27001, HIPAA, GDPR/DPA common Qs & answers and linked to product docs.
- Evidence bundler produces a signed immutable archive with metadata and timestamps.
- CSM SLA estimator returns consistent estimates matching pilot observations within ±20%.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable triage rubric visible in admin console
Template library seeded with SOC2/ISO/HIPAA/GDPR common questions and answers
Evidence bundler produces timestamped archive and manifest

Audit trail maintained for every automated suggestion (user, version, timestamp)
